note.usage: 固定搭配 contingent on/upon；常用於正式文件和商業交易。

noteEn.meaning: Depending on something else happening first.
noteEn.usage: Use 'contingent on' or 'contingent upon'; it is formal.

noteEs.exampleTr: La oferta de trabajo depende de un control médico.
noteEs.meaning: que depende de otra cosa para ocurrir.
noteEs.usage: Se usa contingent on/upon; es lenguaje formal.

noteJa.exampleTr: その採用は健康診断の結果次第だ。

noteJa.usage: contingent on/upon の形で使う。正式な文書でよく見る。

note.usage: 常見 disclose details/the price/information；否定形容詞 undisclosed 表示「未公開的」。

noteEn.meaning: To make secret information known to the public.
noteEn.usage: Common with 'information' or 'the price'; 'undisclosed' means not made public.

noteEs.exampleTr: La empresa se negó a revelar cuánto pagó.
noteEs.meaning: hacer pública una información que estaba oculta.
noteEs.usage: Se dice disclose information/the price; undisclosed = no revelado.

noteHi.exampleTr: कंपनी ने यह बताने से इनकार कर दिया कि उसने कितना भुगतान किया।

noteJa.exampleTr: その会社はいくら支払ったかの開示を拒んだ。
noteJa.meaning: 隠されていた情報を公式に明らかにすること。
noteJa.usage: disclose information / the price の形が多い。undisclosed は「非公開の」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 회사는 얼마를 지불했는지 밝히기를 거부했다.

do.ex: What should I do with these old books?

dr.en: short for Doctor, used before a name

estimate.en: to guess a number or value carefully

exact.ex: I don't know the exact time of the meeting.

executive.en: a senior manager of a company

expanded.en: grew larger; spread into new places

example.zh: 這個專案需要一位具備數據專長的人。

note.meaning: 在某領域的專業知識或技能。
note.usage: 不可數名詞；常見 expertise in sth、technical expertise、bring/provide expertise。

noteEn.meaning: Special skill or knowledge in a particular area.
noteEn.usage: It is uncountable; say 'expertise in something'.

noteEs.exampleTr: El proyecto necesita a alguien con experiencia en datos.
noteEs.meaning: conocimientos o habilidades especiales en un campo.
noteEs.usage: Es incontable; se dice expertise in algo.

noteHi.meaning: किसी क्षेत्र में विशेष ज्ञान या कौशल।

noteJa.meaning: ある分野の専門的な知識や技能。
noteJa.usage: 不可算名詞。expertise in ～ の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 이 프로젝트에는 데이터 전문 지식을 가진 사람이 필요하다.

note.meaning: 使某事更容易進行或發生；促進。
note.usage: 正式用語；受詞通常是事物（facilitate trade/growth），不是人。

noteEn.meaning: To make something easier to happen.
noteEn.usage: It is formal; the object is usually a thing, e.g. 'facilitate trade'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las buenas carreteras facilitan el comercio entre regiones.
noteEs.meaning: hacer que algo sea más fácil o posible.
noteEs.usage: Es formal; el objeto suele ser una cosa (facilitate trade).

noteHi.meaning: किसी काम को आसान बनाना या बढ़ावा देना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 良い道路は地域間の貿易を促進する。

health.en: the condition of the body; medical services

healthcare.ex: Healthcare costs keep rising every year.

healthspan.en: part of the name Healthspan Partners

help.ex: Volunteers help older people with shopping.

hospitals.en: places where sick people are treated

income.en: money a person or company receives

paragraphs: Centric Health runs the biggest group of family doctors in Ireland. It has 90 clinics and 420 GPs. More than 700,000 patients use its doctors.
Now an American company will buy it. The buyer is called Healthspan Partners. It is linked to Bon Secours Mercy Health. Bon Secours already has hospitals in Ireland.
The price is a secret. But people in the business think it is about €350 million. Officials must agree to the deal first.
Two doctors started Centric in 2003. It now also has clinics in the Netherlands and Germany. The company says patients do not need to do anything. Their doctors will stay the same.

An American health group has agreed to buy Centric Health, the largest network of GP practices in Ireland. People in the industry believe the deal is worth around €350 million, but the two companies did not share the price.

The buyer is Healthspan Partners, which is linked to the US group Bon Secours Mercy Health. Bon Secours already runs hospitals in Dublin, Cork, Galway, Limerick and Tralee. The deal still needs approval from the competition regulator and other authorities.

Centric was started in 2003 by two doctors, Maurice Cox and Ray Power. Today it has 90 locations in Ireland, with 420 GPs and more than 700,000 patients. It also has practices in the Netherlands and clinics in Germany. In 2024, its income was almost €144 million, up 13.5 per cent.

Dr Cox will stay as chief executive. He said the new owner would bring experience, international contacts and money to help the company grow. Centric told patients that nothing will change for them, and its practices will keep their name and their independence.

Centric Health, the biggest player in Ireland's primary care market, has agreed to be taken over by a US healthcare group in a deal that industry sources value at about €350 million. Neither side has disclosed the exact price.

The buyer, Healthspan Partners, is an affiliate of Bon Secours Mercy Health, and Bon Secours already operates hospitals in Dublin, Cork, Galway, Limerick and Tralee. The acquisition requires clearance from the Competition and Consumer Protection Commission and other regulators.

Founded in 2003 by doctors Maurice Cox and Ray Power, Centric now operates from 90 sites across the Republic, where 420 GPs serve more than 700,000 patients. It has since expanded into the Netherlands and Germany, although Ireland still generates around 80 per cent of its business. Turnover reached €143.9 million in 2024, a rise of 13.5 per cent.
Dr Cox, who will remain chief executive and a shareholder, said the new owner would provide expertise, global networks and financial backing for further growth, including digital innovation.
Patients have been told they do not need to take any action. The company insists its practices will keep the Centric brand and full clinical independence.

Ireland's largest network of GP practices is poised to change hands, after Centric Health agreed to be acquired by an American healthcare group. Although the terms remain undisclosed, industry insiders put the price tag in the region of €350 million.

The purchaser, Healthspan Partners, is a US affiliate of Bon Secours Mercy Health; the Bon Secours name is already familiar in Ireland, where it runs hospitals in Dublin, Cork, Galway, Limerick and Tralee. The transaction is subject to scrutiny by the Competition and Consumer Protection Commission and other watchdogs.

Established in 2003 by doctors Maurice Cox and Ray Power, Centric has grown into a sprawling operation of 90 sites, where 420 GPs care for upwards of 700,000 patients. It has also ventured into the Netherlands and Germany, yet Ireland still accounts for roughly four-fifths of its revenue, which climbed 13.5 per cent to €143.9 million in 2024.

Dr Cox, who is staying on as chief executive and retaining a stake, said the company harboured significant ambitions and had sought a partner capable of providing expertise, international reach and financial firepower.
Patients have been assured that they need do nothing, while practices will retain the Centric brand and full operational and clinical autonomy.

Centric Health, which is the largest provider of GP services in Ireland, has agreed to be acquired by an American healthcare organisation. Although the price has not been officially disclosed, industry sources estimate that the transaction is worth approximately €350 million.

The acquiring company, Healthspan Partners, is affiliated with Bon Secours Mercy Health, and Bon Secours already operates hospitals in Dublin, Cork, Galway, Limerick and Tralee. Nevertheless, the acquisition is contingent upon approval from the Competition and Consumer Protection Commission and other relevant regulators.

Since its establishment in 2003, Centric has expanded substantially. It currently operates 90 locations, where 420 GPs provide care for more than 700,000 patients. Moreover, it has extended its operations to the Netherlands and Germany, although approximately 80 per cent of its revenue is still generated in Ireland. In 2024, its turnover increased by 13.5 per cent to €143.9 million.

Dr Maurice Cox, a co-founder, will continue as chief executive. He stated that the new owner would provide expertise, global networks and financial resources, thereby facilitating geographical expansion and digital innovation.
Consequently, patients have been informed that no action is required on their part, and the practices will retain both their brand and their clinical independence.
